Generator summary, 22 September 2026: ICCC range entries 160, distinct codes 160, absent at the declared behaviour (3) 70, usable 90, (code,behaviour) records 90 -- all five numbers match the contract's own pre-verified figures exactly. 'Absent at the declared behaviour' means absent at behaviour 3, not absent from ICD-O-3.2 altogether -- the same wording trap recorded in the Group 5 metadata for 9514, and in Group 4 for 8683 (contract §0.3). Eleven of those 70 absent-at-behaviour-3 codes are REDCap options the tool cannot emit (contract §2A) -- ten behaviour exclusions and one deleted number, the first retired ICD-O-3.2 number this project has met in a live REDCap option list: 8965 Nephrogenic adenofibroma -- DELETED in ICD-O-3.2 (IARC 'Deleted codes and their terms', 9 Oct 2020); moved to 9013/0, zero rows for 8965 in icdo32.sqlite. 8966 Renomedullary interstitial cell tumor -- behaviour 0 only; Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places it at 8966/0. 8967 Ossifying renal tumor -- behaviour 0 only; Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places ossifying renal tumour of infancy at 8967/0. 8325 Metanephric adenoma -- behaviour 0 only; Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places it at 8325/0. 8361 Juxtaglomerular tumor -- behaviour 0 only; Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places it at 8361/0. 9013 Adenofibroma, NOS -- behaviour 0 only; Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places metanephric adenofibroma at 9013/0. 8040 Small cell carcinoma, NOS (REDCap's label) -- mislabelled and out of behaviour: ICD-O-3.2's 8040 is 'Tumorlet' at behaviours 0 and 1 only; the entity REDCap's label names, small cell carcinoma NOS, is actually 8041/3, offered separately in the same REDCap list and built as a Tier B entry in this file. 8053 Squamous cell papilloma, inverted -- behaviour 0 only. 8060 Squamous papillomatosis -- behaviour 0 only. 8191 Embryonal adenoma -- behaviour 0 only. 8561 Adenolymphoma -- behaviour 0 only. The test applied throughout is the one Jay's ruling and the Group 3/4/5 contracts already establish: a code leaves the decision tree only when no current WHO entity lives on its stem at the group's declared behaviour, never merely because ICD-O-3.2 prints no usable term at some OTHER behaviour (contract §0.6). Full detail, including the three ICD-O-3.2 additions the inventory carries that REDCap does not (8023, 8054, 8482) and the eight REDCap-string drifts the exact-string check is expected to report, is in the Group 6 build contract §2 and, for the REDCap-facing repair package, in docs/group_06_layer1_repair.md (not authored by this task).

ICD-O-3.2 preferred term 'Neoplasm, malignant', behaviour 3, no [obs] marker; synonyms 'Blastoma, NOS', 'Tumor, malignant, NOS', 'Cancer', 'Malignancy', 'Unclassified tumor, malignant'. This is the group-wide fallback under Visser rule 5: Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rule 5 -- anything not in the paper's Table 3 or Table 4, diagnosed without pathology, is 8000/3, unless a coding expert at the registry rules otherwise (contract §0.11 point 3). A renal mass that fails the nephroblastoma imaging constellation (contract §4.2) and has no tissue in the file is 8000/3 at C64.9, ICCC-3 subgroup VIc -- that is what VIc is for. ★ Router status, contract §3.4 -- CLOSED during this build by a concurrent commit, not by this script: data/shared/presentation_router.json's dual_group_rules['8000-8005'] now carries a 'C64.9' -> {group: 6, subgroup: 'VIc'} branch, listed above the Group XII default, using the 'topography_in' shape app.js's branchMatches() actually reads (commit d205d79, 'Four router branches were dead, two of them across a group boundary', 22 Sep 2026 -- the same commit found and fixed the related dead-branch defect on 8963, recorded on that entry's topography_routing_note). A malignant renal neoplasm NOS can now reach Group VI through the router; group_id 6 in presentation_router.json's own groups map still reads built: false with no tree, so the clerk-facing path through a Group VI document_inventory gate is not yet wired end-to-end -- that remains the next task's work, not a router gap. ICD-O-3.2 preferred term 'Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome-associated renal cell carcinoma', behaviour 3; this stem's [obs] marker sits on the DIFFERENT behaviour, 8311/1 'Hypernephroid tumor' -- a code outside this group's behaviour-3 declaration and outside this entry -- not on the 8311/3 term this entry emits. ICD-O-3.2 created 8311/3 as a new code in the 3.2 revision: '3.1 to 3.2 -- New codes and their terms', p. 5, lists 8311/3 among the new codes, with the HLRCC preferred term and the succinate dehydrogenase-deficient related term both new in 3.2 (contract §0.6, §0.5). ★★ Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places seven WHO 2022 entities on 8311/3: Eosinophilic solid and cystic renal cell carcinoma; TFE3-rearranged renal cell carcinoma; TFEB-altered renal cell carcinoma; ELOC (formerly TCEB1)-mutated renal cell carcinoma; Fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma; Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome-associated renal cell carcinoma; and Succinate dehydrogenase-deficient renal cell carcinoma. Contract §4.3 point 3 additionally records that ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma (Argani P, Genes, Chromosomes and Cancer 2021;60(3):219-227), which shares the sickle-cell-trait predilection otherwise associated with renal medullary carcinoma, also codes 8311/3. ★ This is the contract's §0.5 correction and the single highest-value entry in this file. The diagnostic pathway document's §4F and §7.6 state that these molecularly defined carcinomas 'all collapse to 8312 (RCC NOS)' because 'the registry code set has no distinct codes' for them, and instruct capturing them as annotation only. That is wrong and understates the registry's own code set: ICD-O-3.2 created 8311/3 for exactly these tumours and WHO 2022 assigns most of them to it. code_neutral_molecular is false on this entry, and on this entry only in Group VI's paediatric core: molecular findings are code-DEFINING here, not prognostic. The prioritised workup (Cajaiba MM, et al. Cancer 2018;124(16):3381-3389) is TFE3 immunohistochemistry, then TFE3/TFEB break-apart FISH, then fusion FISH, then next-generation sequencing. Both directions of the error are banned (contract §0.5): the tool must not emit 8311/3 on a molecular suspicion the report does not state, and must not emit 8312/3 for a tumour the report names as one of the seven -- routing a molecularly defined carcinoma to the NOS code makes the case look LESS evidenced than it is, the mirror image of overstating evidence and equally a defect, because the registry then cannot count the entity it actually holds (standing rule, contract preamble and §0.5). ★ Registrar item (contract §11.3, §2C): REDCap Options/Group 6 - Renal Tumors.md still offers 8311 under the string 'Hypernephroid tumor [obs]' -- the obsolete 8311/1 term for a different lesion entirely. A clerk picking 8311 today in REDCap reads that obsolete label and has no way to know the code now means HLRCC-associated and other molecularly defined renal cell carcinoma. This is the most consequential single option-file defect the project has found in this group, recorded in the Layer 1 repair package (contract §2C, docs/group_06_layer1_repair.md, not authored by this task).

This code is for renal cell carcinoma that remains genuinely unclassified after workup -- TFE3/TFEB immunohistochemistry, break-apart and fusion FISH, and sequencing have been done, or are not available, and none of them defined the tumour. ICD-O-3.2 preferred term 'Medullary carcinoma, NOS', behaviour 3, no [obs] marker. Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 1 places four WHO 2022 entities on 8510/3: Medullary carcinoma, NOS; SMARCB1-deficient medullary-like renal cell carcinoma; SMARCB1-deficient undifferentiated renal cell carcinoma, NOS; and SMARCB1-deficient dedifferentiated renal cell carcinoma of other specific subtypes. Collecting duct carcinoma (8319/3, entered separately in this file) RETAINS SMARCB1 expression -- that retention is what separates it from every entity on this code, all four of which lose it (contract §4.3 point 2). ★ Registrar correction (contract §4.3 point 1, §5.6): the diagnostic pathway document calls haemoglobinopathy an 'essential diagnostic criterion' for this code. Moch 2022 §2.4 says otherwise, verbatim per the contract: 'Some unclassified RCC cases with medullary phenotype can show complete loss of SMARCB1, but no association with haemoglobinopathies, suggesting that sickle cell is not a prerequisite for this genetic lesion.' That is why WHO 2022 Table 1 puts SMARCB1-deficient undifferentiated RCC, NOS on this code alongside medullary carcinoma proper -- a sickle-negative case with SMARCB1 loss is not thereby excluded from 8510/3; it is a case for the registrar's own age/sickle-cell/ALK fork (contract §4.3, §8 check 4), not an automatic exclusion. A third tumour shares the sickle-cell-trait association without sharing this code: ALK-rearranged renal cell carcinoma (Argani P, Genes, Chromosomes and Cancer 2021;60(3):219-227) also has a predilection for sickle-cell trait but codes 8311/3, not 8510/3 (contract §4.3 point 3, §0.5). ★ clinical_alert is left null for the same Ruling-9 reason recorded on the 8963 entry -- see that entry's coding_note and this file's build report. Clerk-facing content for the next task's terminal, recorded here author-facing: sickle-cell trait or disease is not required to code 8510/3; SMARCB1 (INI1) loss on immunohistochemistry, not haemoglobinopathy status, is the deciding finding, alongside age (contract §4.3).

morphology_entries.imaging_features: An intrarenal mass -- the claw sign, in which a rim of compressed normal renal parenchyma surrounds the tumour -- confirming intrarenal origin, in a large, well-demarcated mass that pushes rather than invades, in a child under five years. This separates nephroblastoma from neuroblastoma, which is extrarenal and encases vessels where nephroblastoma displaces them. Moch 2022's own table (contract §0.4) is adult-weighted and does not cover this; the basis-of-diagnosis authority is Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05: Nephroblastoma, basis 2 (clinical investigation, including imaging), topography C64, morphology 8960/3, Group VI -- the only Group VI row in the table, and basis 2 only, never basis 1 (contract §0.11). The dedicated imaging source for the claw-sign and push-versus-encase features, Chung EM, et al.
